LESSON: FOOD/ PRACTICES

Grade: PP2
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: HEALTH
Topic 2.5: Food/ PRACTICES

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Food/ PRACTICES. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when nutrition, feeding self eating?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES
4. tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: FOOD/ PRACTICES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Food/ PRACTICES helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: FOOD/ PRACTICES
Food/ PRACTICES is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Food/ PRACTICES” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Food/ PRACTICES matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Food/ PRACTICES this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Food/ PRACTICES” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Food/ PRACTICES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Food/ PRACTICES” around your school. (skill: explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Food/ PRACTICES matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Food/ PRACTICES this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Food/ PRACTICES” around your school. (skill: tell why Food/ PRACTICES matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Food/ PRACTICES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Food/ PRACTICES.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Food/ PRACTICES from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Food/ PRACTICES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Food/ PRACTICES?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when nutrition, feeding self eating?
2. Why should we food from other people’s demonstrate washing wash hands before mouth, fruits eating?
3. Why should we eat eating to wash fruits properly?
4. How do we clear eating. dos and don’ts while the feeding area?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Food/ PRACTICES means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Food/ PRACTICES means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Food/ PRACTICES appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
